newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-KOEN SURVIVES UMPIRING ERROR TO HIT CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KOEN SURVIVES UMPIRING ERROR TO HIT CENTURY.

text.p: Opener Louis Koen survived an umpiring error to impress the national selectors with a century for South Africa's A side in a one-day match against India on Thursday.
The 29-year-old Eastern Province batsman scored 105 from 134 balls to help lift his team from 91 for four to 251 for six in their 50 overs.

A 98-run fifth wicket partnership between Koen and Derek Crookes (55) carried South Africa to a healthy total, with 19-year-old wicketkeeper-batsman Mark Boucher lashing 42 not out from 31 balls in the end-of-innings assault
Koen was dropped at short mid-wicket on 19 and received another let-off on 86 when he was called back from the dressing room by India's captain Sachin Tendulkar.
The third umpire had mistakenly flashed up the red light when he had meant to show green as Koen had made his ground in a run-out appeal.
The mistake was radioed to the on-field umpires and Tendulkar allowed Koen to return from the dressing-room.
